pages.text: Ligands split a metal's d orbitals by Δ, from weak-field (halides) to strong-field (cyanide, carbon monoxide). If Δ is less than the energy P it costs to pair two electrons, they spread out (high spin); if more, they pair (low spin). Colour, magnetism and what the complex catches all follow.
